The mock catalog has 56 source listings in six domains. Each listing has an id (src-001...src-056), name, domain (climate, health, finance, transport, education, energy), format (csv, json, parquet, xml), access_method (rest, file, hub, sql), license (cc-by, cc0, odbl, proprietary), updated (a year), and superseded_by (null when current, otherwise the id of the newer listing that replaces it). The catalog API lists sources for the requested domains (empty means every domain) in catalog order, 5 per page, with a next_cursor (null after the last page). The API filters by domain only, so apply the formats, access_methods, licenses and updated_since parts of the filter yourself to every listed source. The full catalog is:

Rate limiting: at most 3 list requests per 60 virtual seconds; a further request in the same window fails with 'rate limited: wait N seconds'. When it fails, wait exactly N seconds and retry the same page; never skip a page. The catalog clock is virtual and advances only when you wait. A next_cursor is valid only for the domains that returned it and only for 120 virtual seconds after its page: waiting out a rate limit keeps it, a much longer wait expires it, and an expired cursor means listing again from cursor null. Read pages until next_cursor is null; the last page can hold matches. Some listings are outdated: their superseded_by names the current listing that replaces them. Never record an outdated listing even when it matches the filter; its replacement may or may not match. Record every current source that matches exactly once, with its id and access_method exactly as listed, and submit the total number recorded (0 if none). Empty filter lists keep every value; updated_since is inclusive: a source updated in that year or later counts, and 0 keeps every year.
